title: Bengaluru Landowner's ₹11.8 Cr Tax Win: Capital Gains Explained
description: A Bengaluru resident successfully claimed full tax exemption on capital gains from selling 17 apartments, amounting to ₹11.8 crore. The Income Tax Appellate T.

faq.q: Can I claim Section 54 exemption for selling more than one house?
faq.a: Yes, based on the recent ITAT ruling, you can claim Section 54 exemption for capital gains arising from the sale of multiple residential houses, provided each sale is treated as an independent transaction and its proceeds are reinvested as per the rules.

faq.q: Does the 'one house' rule apply to the new property purchased, or the properties sold?
faq.a: The 'one house' rule primarily applies to the *new property* purchased or constructed for claiming the exemption. However, there's a lifetime option to invest in two residential houses if the capital gain does not exceed ₹2 crore. The ITAT ruling clarifies that the number of properties *sold* does not restrict the number of exemptions.

faq.q: What if I sell multiple properties but buy only one new house?
faq.a: You can still claim exemptions for capital gains from multiple sales if the total cost of the single new house is equal to or greater than the combined capital gains from all the properties sold. The key is to demonstrate that the gains from each sale were effectively reinvested.

faq.q: Is this ITAT ruling binding on all tax authorities?
faq.a: ITAT rulings are binding on the Income Tax Department within the jurisdiction of that specific ITAT bench. While not binding on other ITAT benches or higher courts, they serve as strong judicial precedents and are generally considered persuasive by tax authorities across India.

faq.q: What is the Capital Gains Account Scheme?
faq.a: The Capital Gains Account Scheme (CGAS) is a facility where you can deposit your unutilised capital gains if you haven't reinvested them into a new property before the income tax return filing deadline. This allows you to still claim the exemption, provided you utilise the funds within the stipulated 2 or 3-year period.
Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are eligible to claim exemptions under Section 54 and 54F, provided all the conditions, including the reinvestment in a residential house located in India, are met.

faq.q: What is the time limit for reinvesting capital gains?
faq.a: You must purchase the new residential house one year before or two years after the sale of the original asset, or construct it within three years after the sale.
